newsitem.title: UK: Foreign investment to Latin countries to rise - DMG.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment to Latin countries to rise - DMG.

text.p: Foreign direct investment into Latin America, already accounting for a sizeable chunk of money going into emerging markets, is likely to continue its sharp rise this year, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Tuesday.

"In 1996, we calculate that 45 percent of all foreign direct investment into emerging markets went to Latin America, against 25 percent in 1993 and 20 percent in 1994," head of emerging markets research Paul Luke said in a stategy paper.
"In 1997, we expect net FDI to Latin America to rise to $40 billion. This is good news for portfolio investors," he added.
Net foreign direct investment last year, at $29.3 billion, was equivalent to 88 percent of Latin America's current account deficit.
In some countries, such as Argentina and Mexico, the investment figure exceeded the current account deficit.
Luke noted that net foreign direct investment in Latin America last year was up 220 percent from 1993.
